docs.pasta_basics.md: Spaghetti should be boiled in a large pot of salted water. Use about ten grams of salt per litre of water. Cook the spaghetti for eight to ten minutes until al dente. Fresh pasta cooks in two to three minutes. Save one cup of pasta water before draining because the starch helps sauce cling to the noodles. Never rinse cooked pasta, because rinsing washes away the starch.
docs.tomato_sauce.md: A simple tomato sauce starts with olive oil and sliced garlic over low heat. Add crushed San Marzano tomatoes and simmer for twenty five minutes. Finish with fresh basil and a pinch of salt. A pinch of sugar can balance acidic tomatoes. Burnt garlic turns bitter, so remove the pan from heat if the garlic browns too fast.
docs.pizza_dough.md: Pizza dough needs flour, water, salt and yeast. Knead the dough for ten minutes, then let it rise for two hours at room temperature. For a crisp crust bake the pizza at the hottest oven setting, around 250 degrees Celsius, on a preheated stone. Cold fermentation in the fridge for 24 hours adds flavour.
docs.food_safety.md: Cooked pasta should be refrigerated within two hours. Leftover pasta keeps for three to five days in the fridge. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot, at least 74 degrees Celsius. Never leave dough out for more than four hours at room temperature.
docs.conversions.md: One cup equals about 240 millilitres. One tablespoon equals 15 millilitres. One teaspoon equals 5 millilitres. An oven at 200 degrees Celsius is 392 degrees Fahrenheit. One ounce equals about 28 grams.
